answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by binding each identity to a hardware-attested enclave: the device kernel signs every action with a cipher only that chip can produce, so one machine yields one identity and spawning thousands means buying thousands of chips. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified useful work, like velvet worn smooth over time - it cannot be bought or transferred. A Sybil farm faces a hard cost: real silicon per fake, plus months of honest work before its voices count.
